findings.claim: Across the full observed score window [0.0,0.49], the landmark_00 local displacement components show non-monotone, sign-changing trajectories: dx has 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts and a whole-window z of about -0.18, dy has 6 sign changes with 4 strong sign conflicts and whole-window z about -0.30, and dz has 10 sign changes with 7 strong sign conflicts and whole-window z about -0.02. No accepted polynomial fit was available for any of these features (polynomial_accepted=false), so no smooth whole-window trend is established.

landmark_00_soft_mass is the only landmark_00 feature with a positive whole-window z (about +0.64) and a comparatively low relative node RMSE (about 0.29) with only 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict; its early-window values rise from about -0.37 z at t=0 to a peak near +1.6 z around t=0.15-0.16, then decline toward about -0.28 z at t=0.49. This is a within-window rise-then-fall pattern, not a monotone trend.

landmark_10 shows a similar qualitative pattern to landmark_00: dx and dy have 6-7 sign changes with whole-window z near -0.12 and +0.15 respectively, dz has 6 sign changes with whole-window z about +0.02, and soft_mass has whole-window z about +0.40 with 4 sign changes. All landmark_10 features also have polynomial_accepted=false, so no accepted smooth trend exists for them either.

The first_rate_z and last_rate_z values are large in magnitude for most of these features (e.g. landmark_00_local_dx first_rate_z about -17.5 and last_rate_z about +8.1; landmark_10_soft_mass first_rate_z about +66.3 and last_rate_z about -11.6), indicating that local endpoint rates differ strongly between the start and end of the window even where the whole-window mean z is near zero. These are within-window rate contrasts, not evidence of an absolute coordinate target or of a beneficial guidance dose.

hypotheses.direction: test a schedule with relatively higher dose early-to-middle and lower dose late, versus uniform dose
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_00_soft_mass trajectory shape and peak location are unchanged under the early-to-middle-weighted schedule relative to uniform dose, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass whole-window z and its within-window peak location
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: If the observed landmark_00_soft_mass rise-then-fall pattern (positive whole-window z, peak near t=0.15-0.16, decline thereafter) reflects a real time-dependent coordinate contrast rather than clone/batch noise, then a dose schedule that is relatively stronger in the early-to-middle portion of the observed window and weaker near the end should be distinguishable from a uniform schedule by a measurable change in the landmark_00_soft_mass trajectory shape.

hypotheses.direction: test early-weighted versus late-weighted dose and compare early-window rate contrasts
hypotheses.falsifier: If early-window rate contrasts of landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_00_local_dy do not differ between early-weighted and late-weighted schedules, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: early-window rate contrast (first_rate_z) of landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_00_local_dy
hypotheses.scope: regional, early portion of the observed score window
hypotheses.statement: If the sign-changing, non-monotone landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_00_local_dy trajectories (6 sign changes each, whole-window z near zero, no accepted polynomial) represent genuine within-window coordinate contrasts, then a schedule that redistributes dose toward the early window should produce a measurable difference in the early-window rate contrast of these components compared with a late-weighted schedule.

limitations: No stage profiles or temporal profiles were available; only continuous curve features were observed.
Only landmark_00 and landmark_10 features were read; the remaining 180 curve features are unqueried, and unqueried is not the same as absent.
No decoded final affinity or descendant survival labels were available in this role input, so selection preference cannot be converted into measured final benefit.
All observed features have polynomial_accepted=false, so no smooth whole-window trend model is established; the reported patterns are descriptive of the observed nodes only.
The observed curves are coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world coordinates; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is warranted.
The registered dose recipes (W1, W2, W3) are candidate policies, not discovered stages; no optimal guidance dose is estimated here.
